findings.title: Addressee continuity
findings.claim: لَكَ keeps the addressee of Musa's promised patience as the same al-Khidr to whom the non-disobedience pledge is directed.
findings.mechanism: The second-person suffix completes the disobedience relation with the person who will observe the promised quality.
findings.reader_payoff: The two halves remain one encounter with one guide.
findings.containment: This is the local addressee relation; it does not make the following noun possessive.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.

findings.title: Bridge to the command-domain
findings.claim: لَكَ bridges the act of disobedience to the open command-domain at the end of the pledge.
findings.mechanism: Its position between أَعْصِي and أَمْرًا moves from the person affected to the matter involved.
findings.reader_payoff: Personal authority is heard before the promise reaches the broad domain of what may unfold.
findings.containment: This is a local word-order effect; it does not add a second command.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.

findings.title: Personal dative authority
findings.claim: لَكَ directs Musa's non-disobedience toward al-Khidr as a person, while the final noun leaves the commanded matter open.
findings.mechanism: The preposition and suffix form the personal complement of the disobedience verb rather than a possessive relation to أَمْرًا.
findings.reader_payoff: Obedience becomes a relation to a guide, not an abstract virtue.
findings.containment: The finding is bounded by this dative and object; it does not define every authority relation.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.

findings.title: Blanket indefinite object
findings.claim: أَمْرًا gives the pledge an open object: Musa covers whatever command, matter, or course falls under the guide's authority.
findings.mechanism: The indefinite accusative closes the negated verb without naming one order, so the domain remains broad.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise is exposed to the whole unfolding encounter rather than one listed instruction.
findings.containment: The breadth is local to the indefinite object and its authority relation; it is not every unrelated matter.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.

findings.title: Command and affair together
findings.claim: أَمْرًا keeps both a directive and the affair unfolding under that directive in view.
findings.mechanism: Its supplied command-affair range meets the negated disobedience frame, covering an order and an event Musa cannot yet interpret.
findings.reader_payoff: Obedience will be tested by what happens as well as by spoken commands.
findings.containment: The two readings remain within the supplied range and are not ranked.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.

findings.mechanism: Negated first-person disobedience takes the personal dative and then an explicit object.
findings.reader_payoff: A translation's single obedience word is revealed as a three-part relation.
findings.containment: The construction describes this pledge; it does not define every form of obedience.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and trusted supplied evidence support this bounded relation.
